content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is a whole‑grain rice that retains its bran layer and germ. Combined with a mix of vegetables it creates a nutritious dish rich in fiber, vitamins, and minerals. It is commonly used in diet plans and Asian‑style meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice keeps more nutrients than white rice because the outer layers are intact.
It has a lower glycemic index, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.
There are over 40 varieties of brown rice, each with distinct flavor and texture.
Originally cultivated in Asia, brown rice is now grown in the United States, Europe, and Africa.
When stored properly in a cool, dry place, brown rice can last up to 6 months.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain gut health.

items.title: Source of magnesium and selenium
items.content: These minerals are essential for muscle function, nervous system health, and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B3, and B6 aid in converting food into energy and support the nervous system.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Helps control blood glucose levels, beneficial for diabetes management and weight control.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients in brown rice protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: Like many grains, brown rice can contain trace amounts of arsenic; rinsing and cooking in excess water reduces exposure.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Phytic acid may hinder mineral absorption; soaking before cooking lowers its level.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to rice.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the rice by boiling, steaming, or using a rice cooker. Mix with broccoli, carrots, bell peppers, peas, or spinach. Add soy sauce, ginger, garlic, or lemon juice for flavor. Serve as a side, in salads, or as a warm main dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store brown rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator to slow fat oxidation. It typically stays fresh for 6–12 months.
